Article 6.3: Common Rule Violations and Consequences

Warren's summary

# Summary: Common Rule Violations and Consequences

Your account fails if your balance hits the trailing drawdown floor, and you must reset or restart. If you hold positions at 4:50 PM EST, your account is immediately liquidated and considered failed. Trading T1 news events in Exhibition or Funded accounts results in immediate liquidation with all profits forfeited and no funding eligibility. Exceeding max contract limits causes immediate account loss through system enforcement or end-of-day review, and copy-trading more than 5 accounts results in all copy-traded accounts losing funding eligibility and requiring a reset.

Violation	Phase	Consequence
Balance hits trailing drawdown floor	All	Account failed: must reset or restart
Holding positions at 4:50 PM EST	All	Account liquidated and considered failed
Trading T1 news events	Exhibition / Funded	Immediate liquidation, profits forfeited, not eligible for funding
Exceeding max contract limits	All	Immediate account loss (system-enforced or EOD review)
Copy-trading more than 5 accounts	All	All copy-traded accounts lose funding eligibility and must be reset
DLL soft breach (Standard MAX)	Eval / Funded	Session lockout: positions flattened. NOT an account failure.
Account balance below min threshold	OG Funded	Cannot withdraw, not a rule violation itself
More than 30% of a trading day's trades held 5 seconds or less (accounts purchased or reset on or after October 22, 2026)	All	Profit from that day's profitable trades held 5 seconds or less is not eligible for payout. NOT an account failure.
More than 30% of a trading session's trades held 5 seconds or less (accounts purchased before October 22, 2026)	All	See Article 3.8
Violation FAQs

Q: If my account is liquidated for a news violation, do I get my profits?

A: No. If you violate the T1 news rule in Exhibition or any funded account, all profits in that account are forfeited. The account is not eligible for funding.

Q: Can a system glitch cause an accidental contract limit breach?

A: The system prevents single-product contract breaches automatically. Breaches only occur when trading two different products simultaneously. These are reviewed at end-of-day if not caught in real time.

Q: What happens if my account fails?

A: Every account is a one-time purchase, so there is nothing to cancel. A failed evaluation means you reset it or buy a new account.
